provenance.readOnlyProbe: opencode --version + `opencode api` GETs against the configured background service (installed pinned binary; no model invocation, no secret-file reads).
provenance.openApiDocument: https://opencode.ai/v2/openapi.json (guidance; not proof of this installation).
provenance.existingLiveHarness: tests/opencode-managed-live.test.ts and tests/managed-sessions.test.ts (opt-in / injected surfaces; skipped without GREMLYN_LIVE_OPENCODE_MODEL).

readOnlyProbes.result: 200; model keys id,providerID,variant; time keys created,updated; location key directory; outcome absent while unsettled
bounded 8s then killed; 0 stdout bytes; no SSE fields; not a safely bounded consumer

facts.fact: The non-interactive run stream's first step_start carries a top-level sessionID usable as the early parent handle.
facts.limitation: The parser (openCodeStreamParentId) reads only the top-level sessionID and rejects nested part.sessionID; proven by unit fixtures, not by a fresh live run in this probe.

facts.fact: A Session.Info record exposes agent and model{providerID,id,variant}.
facts.limitation: agent is mutable current state; the started identity still requires the first-assistant message read.

facts.fact: A Session.Info record exposes time.created and time.updated as epoch-ms numbers; time.idle is optional.
facts.limitation: time.idle was absent on the probed record; its idle semantics are not independently verified and are never treated as a heartbeat.
The --param flag drops query parameters on 2.0.16, so filters must be encoded into the path; attribution must still echo parentID and directory.

facts.fact: GET /api/session/active returns {data:{ses-id:{type:"running"}}}; sessions absent are inactive.
facts.limitation: Documented scope is process-owned FOREGROUND drains; absence means inactive for those drains. Whether every model-backed background:true child appears in the map is unproven (the pinned probe recorded one still running after its parent returned), so the live observer treats absent nonterminal delegated children as unknown/limited, not idle; absence is never a demonstrated stop or safety proof.

facts.fact: Session.Info.outcome is succeeded|failed|interrupted and is absent while execution is unsettled.
facts.limitation: The current explicit terminal outcome is sufficient for display unless the active map affirmatively contradicts it by listing the session active; safety settlement still requires a terminal outcome and fresh active-map absence.

facts.fact: The first assistant message carries the started agent/model, distinct from the mutable session.agent field.
facts.limitation: The live proof is opt-in; the read is bounded root-verified and returns unknown identity when unavailable.
The type filter is applied before pagination; the probe used only limit=1 and did not re-verify order/type filtering live.

facts.fact: A parent can own overlapping foreground and background child sessions, including a late-spawned background child.
facts.limitation: Background attribution is covered by injected settlement tests and the opt-in live harness; this read-only probe observed only the live foreground active map and did not spawn a model-backed background child. Whether a running background:true child appears in the process-owned active map is unproven, so the live observer treats an absent nonterminal child as unknown/limited, not idle.

facts.fact: Child discovery recurses through echoed parentID edges, each verified against parent and directory.
facts.limitation: Depth (16) and node (1024) bounds are Gremlyn presentation/safety bounds, not runtime facts; nested spawning was proven by settlement fixtures, not a new live run here.

facts.fact: GET /api/event exposes an SSE stream of native and plugin events.
facts.limitation: Documented volatile by contract: a slow consumer overflows and fails the stream, and events during disconnection are missed. `opencode api GET /api/event` produced no usable output within an 8s bound and had to be killed, so no safely bounded event subscription exists through the configured CLI. Polling-only fallback is adopted; no event->delegation mapping is verified.

eventTransport.reason: No safely bounded event subscription through the configured CLI; the stream is volatile and event shapes are not verified.
eventTransport.disconnect: Events during disconnection are missed by contract; reconciliation must recover current/available terminal evidence without claiming continuous coverage.
eventTransport.overflow: A slow consumer overflows and fails the stream by contract.
eventTransport.unsupported: No per-event delegation discriminator is documented (V2EventEncoded is an opaque JSON string); mapping events to observed nodes is unverified.
